subject.title: [Bug]: non_deliverable_terminal_turn produces no outbound notification to channel plugins — Octo (and other channels) go silent

question: Should OpenClaw core automatically deliver a sanitized `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` failure notice through the normal outbound path for plugin channels, or should this become an opt-in plugin SDK lifecycle hook?
rationale: Both approaches are plausible, but the choice changes external channel visibility and may expand the public plugin contract, which repository policy treats as a maintainer product/API decision.

options.title: Core-Managed Terminal Failure Notice
options.body: Route a generic, sanitized terminal-failure payload through the existing delivery pipeline when no committed delivery exists, while preserving explicit `message_tool_only`, room-event, and send-policy guardrails in tests.

options.title: Plugin SDK Hook
options.body: Add a narrow hook such as `onNonDeliverableTurn` so channel plugins can decide how to surface the failure, at the cost of opt-in adoption and a new public API surface.

options.title: Keep Channel-Specific Fixes Only
options.body: Leave OpenClaw core unchanged and ask affected plugins such as Octo to fix delivery envelopes or local fallback behavior, accepting that generic plugin channels may still miss this signal.

recommendation.title: Core-Managed Terminal Failure Notice
recommendation.body: Route a generic, sanitized terminal-failure payload through the existing delivery pipeline when no committed delivery exists, while preserving explicit `message_tool_only`, room-event, and send-policy guardrails in tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision turns on the strict `message_tool` privacy policy that steipete authored and the plugin/channel visibility boundary it established.
